{{nihongo|'''Irō Shrine'''|石室神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} at Irōzaki in {{ill|Minamiizu|arz|ميناميزو|ceb|Minamiizu Chō|es|Minamiizu|fa|مینامی‌ایزو|fr|Minamiizu|id|Minamiizu, Shizuoka|it|Minamiizu|ja|南伊豆町|ko|미나미이즈정|ms|Minamiizu, Shizuoka|pl|Minamiizu|ru|Минамиидзу|sv|Minamiizu|tl|Minamiizu, Shizuoka|tr|Minamiizu|uk|Мінамі-Ідзу|ur|منامی اوزو|vi|Minamiizu, Shizuoka|zh|南伊豆町|zh_yue|南伊豆|qid=Q1203741}}, {{ill|Kamo District, Shizuoka|ar|مقاطعة كامو (شيزوكا)|ceb|Kamo-gun (distrito sa Hapon, Shizuoka-ken)|fa|ناحیه کامو، شیزوئوکا|fr|District de Kamo (Shizuoka)|id|Distrik Kamo, Shizuoka|it|Distretto di Kamo (Shizuoka)|ja|賀茂郡|ko|가모군 (시즈오카현)|pl|Powiat Kamo (Shizuoka)|ru|Камо (Сидзуока)|uk|Повіт Камо (Сідзуока)|zh|賀茂郡|qid=Q961511}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}, near the tip of {{ill|Cape Irōzaki|ceb|Irō Zaki|eo|Kabo Irōzaki|fr|Cap Irō|ja|石廊崎|zh|石廊崎|qid=Q11586512}} at the southernmost end of the {{ill|Izu Peninsula|Q822822|qid=Q822822}}. It is also called '''Irō Gongen''' (いろうごんげん) or '''Irōzaki Gongen''' (いろうざきごんげん). It was formerly also said to be called '''Iware-no-Mikoto Shrine''' (いはれのみことじんじゃ). The enshrined deity is now generally said to be Iware-no-Mikoto, but as noted below, this is not entirely certain. It is identified with “Iwarai no Myōjin, Junior Fourth Lower” in the {{ill|Izu Province shrine-rank register|Q17193087|qid=Q17193087}}. {{nihongo|'''Irō Shrine'''|石室神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

The shrine building is constructed above sea caves on top of mast-like pillars and is counted as one of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Seven Wonders of Izu}}.

About 50 meters away at the farthest tip of the cape is '''Kumano Shrine''' (くまのじんじゃ), but in practice the two are often treated as one {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}}, so both are described here together.

== History and legends of Irō Shrine ==
==History==
There are multiple theories about its origin and founding date, and nothing is fully certain. According to shrine tradition, a hall was first built in {{ill|701|ab|701|af|701|am|701 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|701|ar|701|ary|701|arz|701|ast|701|az|701|azb|۷۰۱ (میلادی)|ban|701|bar|701|be|701|be_x_old|701|bg|701|bn|৭০১|bpy|মারি ৭০১|br|701|bs|701.|ca|701|cdo|701 nièng|ceb|701|ckb|٧٠١|crh|701|cs|701|cv|701|cy|701|da|701|de|701|el|701|eml|701|eo|701|es|701|et|701|eu|701|fa|۷۰۱ (میلادی)|fi|701|fo|701|fr|701|frr|701|fy|701|ga|701|gan|701年|gd|701|gl|701|he|701|hi|701|hr|701.|ht|701 (almanak jilyen)|hu|701|hy|701|id|701|ilo|701|io|701|is|701|it|701|ja|701年|jv|701|ka|701|kaa|701|kk|701 жыл|ko|701년|la|701|lb|701|lij|701|lmo|701|lt|701 m.|lv|701. gads|map_bms|701|mdf|701|mg|701|mhr|701|mk|701|mr|इ.स. ७०१|mrj|701 и|ms|701|myv|701 ие|mzn|۷۰۱|nah|701|nap|701|nds|701|new|सन् ७०१|nl|701|nn|701|no|701|nrm|701|nso|701|oc|701|or|୭୦୧|os|701-æм аз|pl|701|pnb|701|pt|701|qu|701|ro|701|ru|701 год|rue|701|sa|७०१|scn|701|sd|701ع|sh|701.|shn|701|si|701|simple|701|sk|701|sl|701|smn|701|sq|701|sr|701|su|701|sv|701|sw|701|tg|Соли 701|th|พ.ศ. 1244|tk|701|tl|701|tly|701|tr|701|tt|701 ел|uk|701|ur|701ء|uz|701|vec|701|vi|701|war|701|wuu|701年|xmf|701|zh|701年|zh_min_nan|701 nî|zh_yue|701年|qid=Q23496}} (Taihō 1, reign of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|Q357246|qid=Q357246}}). At first it housed a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kannon}} image and {{ill|Demon King of the Sixth Heaven|Q13578873|qid=Q13578873|lt=Dairokutenjin}}, and later {{ill|En no Gyōja|Q198946|qid=Q198946}} received an oracle and enshrined Iware-no-Mikoto.

On the other hand, according to the “Origin Record of Irōzan Kongōin” (displayed in the worship hall), when En no Ozunu was exiled to {{ill|Izu Ōshima|Q1070580|qid=Q1070580}} (from Monmu 3, {{ill|699|Q23493|qid=Q23493}}, to Monmu 5, {{ill|701|ab|701|af|701|am|701 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|701|ar|701|ary|701|arz|701|ast|701|az|701|azb|۷۰۱ (میلادی)|ban|701|bar|701|be|701|be_x_old|701|bg|701|bn|৭০১|bpy|মারি ৭০১|br|701|bs|701.|ca|701|cdo|701 nièng|ceb|701|ckb|٧٠١|crh|701|cs|701|cv|701|cy|701|da|701|de|701|el|701|eml|701|eo|701|es|701|et|701|eu|701|fa|۷۰۱ (میلادی)|fi|701|fo|701|fr|701|frr|701|fy|701|ga|701|gan|701年|gd|701|gl|701|he|701|hi|701|hr|701.|ht|701 (almanak jilyen)|hu|701|hy|701|id|701|ilo|701|io|701|is|701|it|701|ja|701年|jv|701|ka|701|kaa|701|kk|701 жыл|ko|701년|la|701|lb|701|lij|701|lmo|701|lt|701 m.|lv|701. gads|map_bms|701|mdf|701|mg|701|mhr|701|mk|701|mr|इ.स. ७०१|mrj|701 и|ms|701|myv|701 ие|mzn|۷۰۱|nah|701|nap|701|nds|701|new|सन् ७०१|nl|701|nn|701|no|701|nrm|701|nso|701|oc|701|or|୭୦୧|os|701-æм аз|pl|701|pnb|701|pt|701|qu|701|ro|701|ru|701 год|rue|701|sa|७०१|scn|701|sd|701ع|sh|701.|shn|701|si|701|simple|701|sk|701|sl|701|smn|701|sq|701|sr|701|su|701|sv|701|sw|701|tg|Соли 701|th|พ.ศ. 1244|tk|701|tl|701|tly|701|tr|701|tt|701 ел|uk|701|ur|701ء|uz|701|vec|701|vi|701|war|701|wuu|701年|xmf|701|zh|701年|zh_min_nan|701 nî|zh_yue|701年|qid=Q23496}}), he reached this place by the divine power of {{ill|Ekādaśamukha|Q11404731|qid=Q11404731|lt=Eleven-faced Kannon of Fearlessness}}. Also, when a great earthquake occurred in Monmu 4 ({{ill|700|Q23494|qid=Q23494}}), a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=dragon}} and a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=white bird}} appeared and protected this place. A villager dreamed that a treasure hall rose from the sea and settled in a cave midway up the cape; when he went to look, a treasure hall had indeed appeared with {{ill|Ekādaśamukha|Q11404731|qid=Q11404731}} enshrined inside. Later, in the {{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879}} era ({{ill|729|Q23561|qid=Q23561}}–{{ill|749|Q23624|qid=Q23624}}), {{ill|Gyōki|Q1136664|qid=Q1136664}} is said to have enshrined Dairokutenjin.

Another influential theory says that {{ill|Yuzuki no Kimi|Q11066250|qid=Q11066250}}, said to be a fifth-generation descendant of {{ill|Qin Shi Huang|Q7192|qid=Q7192}} of {{ill|Qin (state)|as|ছিন ৰাজ্য|azb|قین (دولت)|be|Царства Цынь|bg|Цин (държава)|ca|Estat de Qin|ckb|چین (ویلایەت)|de|Qin (Staat)|eo|Qin (ŝtato)|es|Estado Qin|eu|Qin estatua|fa|ایالت چین (دودمان ژو)|fi|Qin|fr|État de Qin|hi|चिन राज्य (प्राचीन चीन)|hr|Qin (država)|hy|Ցին (թագավորություն)|id|Qin (negara)|it|Qin (stato)|ja|秦|ka|ცინის სამეფო|ko|진 (영성)|lt|Čin|mk|Ќин (држава)|mn|Цинь ванлиг|nl|Qin (staat)|no|Qin (stat)|pl|Qin (okres Zhou)|pt|Reino de Chim|ru|Цинь (царство)|sh|Qin (država)|sv|Qin (stat)|th|รัฐฉิน|tr|Qin (devlet)|uk|Цінь (царство)|ur|چن (ریاست)|vi|Tần (nước)|wuu|秦国|zh|秦国|zh_classical|秦|zh_min_nan|Chîn-kok|zh_yue|秦|qid=Q34756}} who naturalized in Japan (with variant accounts), came to be called Monoi Mina-no-Mikoto, and that this shrine was established by the {{ill|Hata clan|Q987290|qid=Q987290}}, who claimed descent from him, to worship that deity. However, whether this Monoi Mina-no-Mikoto is connected to {{ill|Monoiminanomikoto Shrine|Q11570647|qid=Q11570647|lt=Monoi Mina-no-Mikoto}} enshrined on {{ill|Kōzu-shima|Q301669|qid=Q301669}} in former {{ill|Izu Province|Q860928|qid=Q860928}} remains unclear.

The {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} records an “Iware-no-Mikoto Shrine” in Kamo District, Izu Province. It is generally regarded as this shrine, though another view says this association was attached in later ages.

Afterward it attracted devotion as Kongōzan Ishimuro Gongen under {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}}. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it is said to have received a donation of two hyō of rice from the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tokugawa shogunate}} through the {{ill|Nirayama Daikansho|Q11664099|qid=Q11664099}}. It is also said that the legend of “{{ill|The mast of Irōzaki Gongen|Q11586514|qid=Q11586514}},” associated with this shrine as one of the {{ill|Seven Mysteries of Izu|Q11380538|qid=Q11380538}}, arose in this period.

With the early-{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Meiji}} {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}, it came to be called Irō Shrine. The present shrine building was rebuilt in Meiji 34 ({{ill|1901|Q2035|qid=Q2035}}). It is famed as a deity of maritime safety, business prosperity, and academic success, and as a scenic spot at the tip of the {{ill|Izu Peninsula|Q822822|qid=Q822822}}.

==Legend==
{{main|石廊崎権現の帆柱}}

== Origin and legend of Kumano Shrine ==
A village headman’s daughter named O-Shizu from Nagatsuro near {{ill|Cape Irōzaki|ceb|Irō Zaki|eo|Kabo Irōzaki|fr|Cap Irō|ja|石廊崎|zh|石廊崎|qid=Q11586512}} fell in love with a fisherman named Kōkichi. Because their different status made the relationship unacceptable, Kōkichi was exiled to {{ill|Mikomoto Island|Q11589438|qid=Q11589438}}. Unable to forget him, O-Shizu lit a fire every night at the tip of Irōzaki and confirmed their love with Kōkichi on Mikomoto Island.

One night, worried because she could not see the fire on Mikomoto Island, O-Shizu put out in a small boat, but strong winds raised high waves and she could not advance. She prayed single-mindedly to the gods. By that grace she drifted to Mikomoto Island, and the two safely reunited and were joined. Their parents eventually accepted them, and they are said to have lived happily ever after.

At the place where O-Shizu lit her fire, a small shrine to {{ill|Kumano Gongen|Q11568925|qid=Q11568925}} was enshrined, and it came to be known as a deity of matchmaking. After the early-Meiji separation of kami and buddhas, it came to be called Kumano Shrine.
